raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44913
* __->__ #44912
* #44904
* #44901

## Motivation

`num_fused_shared_experts` carries two meanings: shared experts executed by the fused MoE layer, and shared id/weight slots emitted by ordinary TopK. Waterfill needs fused computation while appending the shared slots after ordinary routing. Conflating these quantities makes TopK and HashTopK rewrite their constructor arguments for Waterfill.

## Modifications

- Keep `num_fused_shared_experts` for the experts-layer layout and use `num_shared_topk_slots` for shared output positions emitted by ordinary routing, before Waterfill expansion.
- Derive ordinary routing slots once in `shared_topk_slots`: the fused count normally, zero when Waterfill writes the slots later. Construct TopK/HashTopK from these meanings directly.
- Update router consumers and layout helpers; retain existing kernel interfaces.
- Guard the single-writer invariant: the router or Waterfill emits the shared slots exactly once, including unfused and empty-output cases.

#44913 places both quantities in one immutable model-owned configuration and exposes it through `get_model().shared_experts`.

## Validation

- Latest naming change (`456745b5ee` → `6a5c963f49`): inverse-renaming yields identical Python ASTs in all 15 changed files. Applicable pre-commit hooks pass.
- At PR1 `6a5c963f49` and PR2 `b500124929`: GLM-4.7-Flash on 2× H200, BF16, TP2, Triton attention/MoE, decode CUDA Graph batches 1/2/4, routed-experts capture enabled. Four sequential greedy requests have identical tokens and expert routes. One of two batched requests varies between repeated PR1 runs; the repeated PR1 run matches PR2 on all six requests.
- Final stack validation on PR2: 51 CPU test files pass, including Waterfill, scaling, HashTopK, fusion policy, capture width and model-scope isolation. Four CUDA routing files pass (31 cases, 7 backend-specific skips).

After integrating #44901 `6c1b70e909` and #44904 `4676743e28`, PR1 `b7f88f502e` passes all 13 scaling CPU tests and all nine CUDA append/remap/runtime-routing tests on one H200 (same libraries as above). The inherited folding-mode and global shared-slot regressions use this PR's slot-count API. Applicable pre-commit hooks pass.

Coverage limits: no full-model Waterfill, fused-draft, distributed DeepEP/MegaMoE, AMD, NPU or XPU run in this validation. The GLM smoke is a limited equivalence check, not an accuracy benchmark.

## CI fixture follow-up at `720d6dbef4`

The [ROCm 10 MI35x job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39124404687/job/117666744625) failed at `faaf4bb4e6` because `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py::_moe_stub` bypasses `DeepseekV2MoE.__init__` and omitted `routed_scaling_factor_fused_in_topk`. The stub now supplies that construction state. The other five test files in that partition passed. This fixes the test fixture; production executable behavior is unchanged.

On one H200, the original fixture reproduces the same AttributeError with the AITER epilogue flags forced; after repair, all four normal/dual-stream and shared-TP1 combinations pass through the actual forward methods. This checks the Python fixture/epilogue contract, not native ROCm collectives or graph replay. The complete AMD TP4 file still needs CI validation.

The kernel comparison now covers normalization and explicit folding independently; the complete standalone router test file passes all 52 cases on one H200. Its stale normalization explanation and CUDA JIT parity claim are corrected. The CUDA counterpart retains its existing unnormalized shared-weight behavior; caller search found tests and benchmarks, with no serving caller.

TopKConfig documents its total ordinary output width and the global AITER absolute shared coefficient versus the standard-path multiplier. Eager/fused subtest labels include the folding mode. Duplicate ordinary model-context scopes and a derived routed-count property remain optional follow-ups. Applicable pre-commit hooks pass. No native AMD rerun or model accuracy result is claimed for this follow-up.

The repaired stack is #44901 `cdf052beb7` → #44904 `beb15ea999` → #44912 `720d6dbef4` → #44913 `5214d477ec`.

## Landing cleanup (2026-10-19)

Current head: `ac55bb9625`, rebased onto main after #44901 and #44904 merged.

Condensed repetitive slot-count and Waterfill explanations without changing executable statements. Configured pre-commit and comment/docstring AST comparisons passed on the cleanup diff. The focused exclusive-writer regression remains in normal CPU CI; broader routing and compile coverage moves to Extra in #44913. Earlier hardware results above retain their recorded revisions; no new accelerator or full-model run is claimed for this cleanup/rebase.
